div.p: employee is a real hr.employee record, so everything the Loans app adds to it is available here. Every expression below was checked against a real payslip.
div.h4: What to deduct for this payslip
div.p: This is what the DED_LOAN rule uses. It counts the actual days the payslip covers, so a 31-day cutoff takes slightly more than a 30-day one.
div.div: Always pass the two dates. Called with no arguments the method assumes one week, so a monthly payslip would deduct roughly a quarter of what is due. And keep the result negative — deductions are stored as negative totals and summed into the Deduction category.

ul.li: employee.loan_balance — total still owed across active loans
employee.loan_cutoff_deduction — the one-week figure, for display
employee.loan_active_count — how many loans are being repaid
employee.loan_unauthorized_count — active loans with no signed authorization, which deduct nothing
employee.loan_max_amount — the configured ceiling at this length of service

div.pre: result = -sum(l.repayment_amount for l in employee.loan_ids if l.state == 'active' and l.deduction_authorized)
div.p: Useful fields on each loan: amount, balance, total_paid, total_payable, repayment_amount, monthly_amortization, interest_amount, state, deduction_authorized, start_date, loan_type_id.
Returns (loan, amount due this period) pairs, oldest first, already filtered for authorization, start date and remaining balance.
div.pre: rows = employee._loan_deductions(payslip.date_from, payslip.date_to) result = -sum(a for _l, a in rows)
due = employee._loan_deduction_total(payslip.date_from, payslip.date_to) result = -min(due, categories.BASIC * 0.20) # never take more than 20% of basic
result_name = 'Loan Repayment (%d active)' % employee.loan_active_count result = -employee._loan_deduction_total(payslip.date_from, payslip.date_to)
div.div: Do not create records from a rule. Odoo blocks it, and it would be wrong anyway: compute_sheet() runs again every time anyone recomputes a draft payslip, so you would post a duplicate repayment on each recompute. Repayments are posted once, when the payslip is confirmed, stamped with its number so re-confirming cannot double-credit, and reversed if it goes back to draft.
If you change the DED_LOAN formula so it no longer matches _loan_deductions(), the repayment allocator will log "N unaccounted for" rather than mis-credit a loan. Check the log after a payroll run.
